title: IPv6-only VPC validation harness and egress-rewrite acceptance criteria
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for a validation harness that runs synthetic traffic and health checks in IPv6-only and dual-stack VPCs, with focused tests for egress rewriting (NAT64/NAT66 proxies, egress proxies) and air-gapped/offline upgrade constraints. Scope: validation tooling, test cases, telemetry targets, rollback criteria during staged operator upgrades, and documentation for customers running IPv6-only private deployments. Out of scope: changes to the operator networking stack or upstream cloud provider features.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can boot a configurable 3-node cluster in an IPv6-only test subnet and run a canonical request profile (chat, embeddings, streaming) against the control plane and data plane without requiring IPv4 fallback.

Egress-rewrite scenarios: harness validates at least three rewrite strategies (NAT64 translation, egress-proxy rewrite, split-horizon DNS rewrite) and reports pass/fail per strategy with clear logs and packet captures available.

Upgrade safety: during a simulated operator upgrade (image churn + config apply) the harness must detect and surface failures within 60s and trigger the documented silent-rollback flow; median detection time observed in tests must be <= 45s.

Telemetry and observability: the test run emits structured telemetry (latency P50/P95/P99, error rate, TLS handshake failures, DNS resolution failures) that is persisted to the private telemetry sink. Minimum telemetry retention for validation runs is 7 days.

Air-gapped acceptance: for an air-gapped deployment (zero egress), the harness validates offline image staging and verifies checksum parity for all operator artifacts. A checksum mismatch must fail the run and surface a remediation ticket template.

Performance gates: IPv6-only paths must meet 90% of equivalent dual-stack median tail latency (P95) for the canonical profile; if a strategy falls below 70% the run is marked 'performance regression' and flagged for engineering follow-up.

Customer-facing docs: acceptance requires a step-by-step runbook (network preconditions, required firewall ACLs, DNS entries, and example tcpdump filters) and an automated artifact that customers can run in their environment to reproduce the validation locally.
Test reproducibility: every harness run must produce an artifacts bundle (logs, pcap, telemetry snapshot, kube-operator events) that can be uploaded to support and linked in the failure ticket.

Non-regression: add the harness as a gate in the private deploy PR pipeline; new operator changes that cause the harness to fail must block the merge of release branches until triaged and a patch is landed.

Security check: the harness must exercise KMS-integrated bootstrap in a simulated air-gapped mode and verify that secrets are never exported in plaintext in any artifact bundle. Any violation fails the run.
test_plan: Step 1: Provision ephemeral infra in the staging VPC (IPv6-only and dual-stack variants) using the private-deploy test harness template.
Step 2: Stage operator artifacts via the offline image mirror flow (simulate air-gap) and validate checksums across nodes.
Step 3: Execute canonical workload generator (mix of small streaming chat + medium embeddings + occasional rerank) for 30 minutes and collect P50/P95/P99 latency and error signals.
Step 4: Run egress-rewrite matrices: NAT64, egress-proxy, split-DNS; validate connectivity to external model mirrors or verify proxy responses in air-gapped mode via mirrored artifacts.
Step 5: Perform a staged operator upgrade (canary -> remainder) and ensure detection and silent-rollback behave according to the upgrade safety criteria.
Step 6: Bundle artifacts and run an automated post-run validator that asserts acceptance criteria and uploads a report to the private telemetry sink.
Step 7: If failures occur, capture a standard failure report and create a triage ticket template with links to relevant artifacts and suggested mitigations.
Step 8: Repeat runs for three different network MTU sizes (standard, small, jumbo) to exercise fragmentation and path MTU behaviors in IPv6-only networks.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal harness development and validation in ENG staging (2 sprints). Phase 2: integrate harness into CI gating for private deployments and run full validation on each release candidate. Phase 3: publish runbook and customer-facing artifact; offer a 'self-validate' script in customer onboarding. Each phase gated by 'acceptance_criteria' items 1-5.
open_questions: Q1: Should the harness natively simulate ISP-level DNS64 behavior or rely on a standalone NAT64 service? Decision pending network infra input.
Q2: For air-gapped checksum validation, do we require signed images (image-signing integration) or is SHA256 parity sufficient for initial rollout?
Q3: Who will own the private telemetry sink for validation runs in long-term (SRE or Product)? Need resource commitments for retention and access controls.
decisions: D1: Initial rollout will support three egress strategies (NAT64, egress-proxy, split-horizon DNS); provider-specific NAT64 emulation will be added later.
D2: Use SHA256 parity for Phase 1 air-gap validation; image-signing integration will be scoped as a separate initiative with Security.
D3: SRE will host the private telemetry sink for validation artifacts with RBAC-scoped read access for support and engineering.
updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff meeting with Networking and SRE. Agreed owner for telemetry sink (SRE).
2025-02-12: ENG spike completed for NAT64 emulation; prototype can emulate basic translation but requires more DNS behavior simulation.
2025-02-14: Design review with Security: image-signing added to backlog; phase-1 will use SHA256 parity. Security requested automated secret-scrubber for artifacts bundle.
2025-02-15: PM review approved acceptance criteria with minor wording edits; assigned to Diego for implementation planning.
